output.summary: Under Mandate 2038’s Default Game, a four-Era game uses a thirteen-tile modular board, four Era decks, a 50-card Training deck, and twelve Era Mandates. Each player selects three of six Core Actions per Era, resolving simultaneous choices clockwise from Initiative through Select → Move → Act. The institution with the most Mandate wins; the shared World Ending is resolved separately. Tactics and secret objectives are not used.
keyRules: Suggested player count is 3–5; Default Game lasts four Eras: Progress, Capacity, Authority, and Continuity.
Advanced Play is an all-game extension selected before setup; this chunk does not provide its procedures. In Default Game, use Headline cards without an Advanced Play badge.
Build the thirteen-tile board with Frontier in the center, six shuffled operational tiles in the surrounding ring, and six shuffled public tiles in evenly spaced outer positions.
Separate Headline cards by Era, shuffle the Default-eligible cards, reveal three per Era, and leave space for a twelve-card Future Timeline.
Shuffle the Training deck. Divide the twelve Era Mandates into four shuffled three-card Era decks beside the matching Era cards.
Place shared Runway, Compute, Safety, Scrutiny, Systemic Risk, Joint Venture, Mega-Cluster, Initiative, and Audit-bag components within reach, with Power Source references nearby.

Each player takes their faction materials and starting resources. Place each CEO and one Team at Frontier; keep two Teams in supply. Set Runway, Compute, Capability, Customers, Trust, and Safety to printed starting values.
Place each faction’s already-earned public Mandate on the shared track as printed. Put all ten Scrutiny cubes from each faction outside the empty Audit bag.
Add all factions’ printed starting Trust and record the fixed total as Setup Collective Trust on the Era reference; it is used during the World Ending.
Choose Initiative randomly. Begin Era I.

Each player has six Core Actions—Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, Influence—but takes only three turns per Era. Select three different Core Actions in any order; played Core Actions remain exhausted until the next Era unless readied.

An ordinary turn proceeds: reveal one Headline; secretly select one unused Core Action or spend one Escalation availability for one unlocked Escalation; reveal simultaneously; resolve clockwise from Initiative; select one acting piece; move it zero, one, or two adjacent hexes; resolve the selected Action from the destination; exhaust the Core Action or spend and flip the Escalation; pass Initiative clockwise before the next cycle. A revealed Action cannot be replaced after selection even if it becomes blocked after reveal. The player must choose legal piece, movement, mode, target, payment, and immediate trade options during resolution if available, otherwise the Action remains committed and becomes blocked as applicable; exact blocked-action consequences need the continuation rules if not stated later in the source set. A Headline is revealed once per turn and grants no additional Action unless another rule says otherwise, which is not established here; Headline effects change one named field or invoke one public-choice procedure. Readying resolves nothing immediately and only makes a card available for a later choice. Agent Swarm is the sole compound-action exception identified here; it resolves and exhausts two different unused Core Actions, requiring its detailed card/procedure reference for full resolution. An acting piece is a CEO or Team: CEO contributes two presence and Team one. Both may take any Action. Facilities and Generators cannot act. The destination controls where Facilities and power infrastructure may be built, where Research and Deploy occur, which location bonus applies, and which political spaces may be Influenced. Organize receives ordinary movement before its additional movement, recruitment, restructuring, or relocation. Effect precedence is Era global unlocks, faction-board modifiers, current Headline global effect, then the ordinary Action plus one destination bonus, one faction modifier, and applicable global effects. Exceptions are timed before selection, during movement, during action, or after action. Era systems are inactive until listed under New this Era; read that strip aloud before revealing the Mandate. Era cards, Escalations, and faction abilities are open information. Progress teaches ordinary institutional work; Capacity adds industrial infrastructure; Authority adds agreements, quantum record disputes, and public effects; Continuity adds compound Actions, declarations, and exceptional generation. Later Eras retain prior systems unless an effect says otherwise. Whenever an effect targets the lowest, highest, or most of something, tied players are resolved by nearest Initiative clockwise unless the effect explicitly affects or awards all tied players. Initiative is an order, not a resource: it cannot be traded or retained, and passing it changes resolution order and unresolved ties. Escalation availability is tracked on the faction board. Availability is spent to select unlocked Escalations, committed on selection, reduced by one, and expires at Era end if unspent. Each named Escalation is usable once per player per game; previously unlocked unused Escalations remain available in later Eras. Era I grants 0 availability and no Escalations; Era II grants 1 and unlocks Mega-Cluster and Reorganization; Era III grants 1 and unlocks Open Weights and Narrative Capture; Era IV grants 2 and unlocks Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Global after movement means normal movement occurs, then the Action resolves without a destination restriction.

rulesReconstruction: Each Era has three cycles. A Headline is revealed and resolved in each cycle, with resolved cards retained in the Era’s Future Timeline.
Players negotiate, select one Core Action secretly, resolve actions, conduct power allocation and Production, then award threshold-based Mandate during the Era’s progression.

The six Core Actions—Research, Fund, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence—are available according to Era and system unlocks; illegal or unavailable choices become no-ops or require fallback resolution.

Movement is limited to 0–2 shared-edge steps. Rival pieces may coexist; Facilities cannot occupy Frontier; Generators require an Energy hex and available slot; Organize and Facility movement require adjacent legal destinations.
Grid-Ready status is checked during Production and can be lost through relocation, loss of Power eligibility, or inadequate Power. Final offline Facilities cost 1 Mandate each, never below zero.

Scrutiny is player-colored, capped at ten cubes per player before Runway or Trust must substitute, and Public Audit draws an Era-scaled number of cubes. Era-IV colored cubes and black Systemic Risk have special penalties.
Power can be bought and sold through negotiation, and Production determines which Facilities are powered, satisfied, and networked.
Fusion Demonstrator is a late strategic option requiring Power Corridor, 5 Runway, 6 Power construction, 2 Mandate, and 3 Scrutiny.
